newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says Lebed dismissal not a "turning point".
newsitem.headline: U.S. says Lebed dismissal not a "turning point".

text.p: The United States said on Thursday that the sacking of Russian security chief Alexander Lebed did not appear to be "a fundamental turning point" and the Russian government was stable.

State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said it was not approriate for Washington to comment on an internal decision by President Boris Yeltsin, but added: "I don't think the American public needs to worry that this is some fundamental turning point."

Burns said: "This is dramatic. It's important. We're not exactly sure where it's going to lead in the future but the (U.S.-Russian) relationship is stable and this is what matters ultimately to the American people."
Speaking at a regular State Department briefing, Burns said: "The Russian government is stable, led by President Yeltsin..."

He said U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry, who is visiting Russia, was told about Lebed's dismissal "a couple of minutes" before Yeltsin's announcement. Perry had been due to meet Lebed about that time and put the meeting off.

He said the Clinton administration was confident it could work with Yeltsin's government on issues including securing ratification of the Start II nuclear weapons treaty which is the subject of Perry's trip. "We're not going to stop now because of a little political turmoil in Moscow," he added.
